Thought: To find the absolute bioavailability (F) of a drug, we use the formula:

\[ F = \frac{\text{AUC}_{\text{oral}} \times \text{Dose}_{\text{IV}}}{\text{AUC}_{\text{IV}} \times \text{Dose}_{\text{oral}}} \]

Given:
- \(\text{AUC}_{\text{oral}} = 0.12 \, \text{mg} \, \text{h}^{-1} \, \text{L}^{-1}\)

- \(\text{Dose}_{\text{oral}} = 3 \, \text{mg}\)
- \(\text{Dose}_{\text{IV}} = 3 \, \text{mg}\)

Substitute these values into the formula to calculate F:

\[ F = \frac{0.12 \times 3}{0.18 \times 3} \]

The doses cancel out, simplifying the equation to:

\[ F = \frac{0.12}{0.18} \]
